# dsh-schedule-send
**English** | 中文
Schedule-send for DeepSeek Harness: write a message in the composer, pick a time, and the text is de
livered into the **same conversation** later as a **normal user message** — exactly as if you had pr
essed Send at that moment, so the agent answers it and the thread continues.
## Features

- A clock control in the composer tool row, beside the send button.
- Quick picks (30 minutes, 1 hou

r, 3 hours, tomorrow 09:00) or an exact local date and time.
- The draft is cleared immediately; a p

ersistent card in the conversation records what is queued, when it sends, and offers **Cancel**.
- D
urable queue outside the workspace, with catch-up: a send that came due while the app was closed is

delivered on the next start.
- The delivered text is a real user message (`source.kind = 'user'`), n

ot a reminder or a system notice.
- Retries with exponential backoff; the send id doubles as the pro

mpt `requestId`, so a retry after a crash cannot deliver twice.
- No build step and no runtime depen
dencies beyond the page's shared `react` / `react-dom`.
## Why not the built-in reminders?
DSH's built-in Schedule subsystem is a reminder system: it injects a `[SCHEDULE REMINDER]` framing t
hat tells the model to **present** the text to the user instead of treating it as an instruction. A
scheduled send needs the opposite semantics — the text must become the user's message and start a tu
rn. This plugin therefore keeps its own durable queue and delivers through the public `ctx.sessionCo
ntroller.prompt(...)` seam, which resumes a cold session when needed and mints an ordinary user mess
ller.prompt(...)` seam, which resumes a cold session when needed and mints an ordinary user message.
## Install
The package declares both a Host half (`index.js`, which owns the queue, the commands, and delivery)
and a browser half (`client.js`). There is no build script, so every route installs finished files.

### Option 4: the Web UI
Open the sidebar's **Plugins** page, choose to install a bundle, and paste one of the specs above (`
github:Zhiyi-Zhao/dsh-schedule-send`, a tarball URL, or an absolute path). Installing from the runni
ng app needs `danger-full-access` permission or an approval.
> `--profile desktop` names the desktop app's profile. A `dsh web` deployment uses `--profile web`;
the bundle works in any profile that composes the Web client. Replace `desktop` with your profile na
me in every command below.
After installing into the desktop profile, the new bundle can apply through HMR; if it does not appe
ar, restart DeepSeek Harness. Uninstall with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Usage

1. Type the message in any conversation (plain text).
2. Click the clock button to the left of Send.

3. Pick a quick time, or set an exact local date and time.
4. Confirm with **Schedule**. The draft

is cleared and a "Scheduled send" card appears in the conversation.
5. At the chosen time the messag
e is delivered into that conversation as a normal user message; the agent answers it. **Cancel** on
the card works until delivery.
The card stays in the transcript as history. After delivery, Cancel reports that the message already
n the transcript as history. After delivery, Cancel reports that the message already left the queue.
> The package also registers two internal session commands (`schedule-send`, `schedule-send-cancel`)
because the session command channel is how a browser plugin reaches its Host half. They appear in t
he slash menu; you never need to type them — the clock control is the interface.
## How it works
| Step | Where | What happens |
| Create | Browser | The composer control calls `ctx.remote.commands.execute('/schedule-send <json>'

)` with the message, the target epoch, an id, and the browser's IANA zone. |
| Persist | Host | The
command handler validates the payload and writes a record to `$DSH_HOME/schedule-send/queue.json` (a

tomic temp-file rename). |
| Sweep | Host | A 5-second sweep picks due records and calls `ctx.sessio

nController.prompt({ requestId: id, sessionId, mode: 'queue', content, clientTimeZone })`. |
| Deliv
er | Host | That public method resumes the session if needed and submits a normal user message; the

send id is the dedupe key, so retries are idempotent. |
| Feedback | Browser | The command lifecycle
renders as the persistent card through a `conversation.chat.commandview` renderer keyed by the comm
the persistent card through a `conversation.chat.commandview` renderer keyed by the command name. |
## Verified delivery
One real scheduled send, read back from the Host queue (local time, Europe/Copenhagen):
| Field | Value |

| status | `delivered` |
| created | 2026-10-19 12:22:16 |
| target | 2026-10-19 12:24:00 |
| delive

red | 2026-10-19 12:24:03 |
| delay | 3.2 s (inside the 5 s sweep interval) |
The delivered text appeared in the conversation as a normal user message and the agent answered it t
elivered text appeared in the conversation as a normal user message and the agent answered it there.
## Compatibility
Verified against DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** in the desktop app.
- Host half: `ctx.commands.register`, `ctx.sessionController.prompt`, `ctx.sessions.flush`, `ctx.age

nts` — public services only.
- Browser half: the slot API (`conversation.input.right`, `conversation
.chat.commandview`), the locale service, and `ctx.remote.commands.execute`; it imports only `react`

and `react-dom`, not DSH UI primitives, so minor UI-package changes do not break it.
- If `ctx.sessi
onController` is absent, scheduled sends stay queued and a warning is logged instead of failing the
ller` is absent, scheduled sends stay queued and a warning is logged instead of failing the profile.
